2.1.
On 19.08.2011, criminal proceedings were initiated against the petitioners by the Food Inspector, through a complaint registered as Criminal Case No. 3215/2014.

The complaint, filed in the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jalore, alleged violations under Section 7(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Act,
punishable under Section 16 of the Act.
2.2. On 28.03.2011, the Food Inspector inspected M/s Ganpati Stores and found 25 sealed packets of "Sugar Boiled Confectionary."
He collected three sample packets for analysis, which were subsequently labeled with code 0-1402.

Two sets of these samples were sent to the Local Health Authority and Chief Medical and Health Officer, Jalore, on 29.03.2011, while one set was forwarded to the Food Analyst at the Public Health Laboratory, Jodhpur, on 04.04.2011.
2.3. The Public Analyst's report dated 05.05.2011 indicated that the sample was adulterated, as it did not meet the standards under the PFA Rules.
Specifically, the "Ash insoluble" content was 0.38%, exceeding the permissible limit of 0.2%.
2.4. On 22.06.2011, the Food Inspector asked for details from the petitioners, who responded on 30.07.2011, clarifying that they were not the manufacturers of the product in question.

The actual manufacturer was identified as "M/s Leamak Healthcare Pvt.
Ltd., Ahmedabad."
[2024

. Notwithstanding, a sanction order was issued on 29.07.2011 by the Local Health Authority, Jalore, authorizing the prosecution of the petitioners in a vague manner under Section 7(1) read with Section 16 of the PFA Act.

Subsequently,
on 19.08.2011, the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate of Jalore took cognizance of the complaint.
Hence, the instant petition.

3. Having heard learned counsel for the petitioners, it transpires that during pendency of the instant petition, although an interim order was granted by a co-ordinate bench of this Court staying further trial proceedings qua the petitioners, but the same has turned out to be self goal.

The other co-accused, who were proceeded with by the trial court, were acquitted on the grounds of non-compliance of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act by the complainant/prosecution.
However, due to the stay granted in favor of the petitioners in the present proceedings, they were not accorded the same benefit, and as a result, the trial remains pending against him.
Case of the petitioners is stated to be absolutely pari materia with other co accused.

4. In the aforesaid premise, the instant petition is disposed of with the expectation that, upon the petitioner appearing before the learned trial court with a webprint copy of this order, appropriate steps will be taken to extend the same benefit that has already been granted to the co-accused,
provided the petitioners are found entitled to it.

6. The petitioner no.1 is stated to be a resident of Gurugram (Haryana), and the complaint pertains to the year 2011, and at that time he was employed with petitioner no.2. company.
The complaint was filed against him for certain alleged deficiencies in performance of his official duties.

Since then,
he has left his employment with the company.
Given the considerable distance, it is understandable that he may face difficulty in appearing before the learned trial court.

Therefore, it is directed that the petitioner shall be allowed to be represented by an authorized representative before the learned trial court, upon his filing an appropriate application in accordance with the law.
7. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
